name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: CVE-2026-8037 — Progress LoadMaster Command Injection Vulnerability
items.dek: Progress LoadMaster. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 10 August.

items.title: Hardware Keystores for AI Agent Signing Workflows: A Zero-Trust MCP Enforcement Architecture
items.dek: Hardware keystores via PKCS#11 prevent agent private-key exfiltration in Git and API workflows; zero-trust MCP enforcement stack.
items.unproven: deployment at scale in containerized CI/CD; HSM/TPM availability and cost trade-offs in financial services; taint-tracking effectiveness across framework boundaries.

items.title: The Vulnerability With No CVE: Managing Persistent Gaps Between Mandate and Authority in AI Coding Agents
items.authors: Shayell Aharon Salomon Amir Shaked Matan Noga
items.dek: Agentic Posture Vulnerability (APV) framework operationalizes persistent agent-control exposure tracking across components.
items.unproven: integration with existing vulnerability-management platforms; field validation beyond vignette; automation of APV detection and closure verification.

items.title: When Experience Becomes Instruction: Trajectory Poisoning in Self-Evolving Agent Skill Systems
items.dek: Trajectory-poisoning attack embeds malicious behaviors into self-evolving LLM agent skills at 91% success rate across six mainstream evolvers.
items.unproven: Limited to closed-world skill banks and LLM families tested; unclear if mitigations exist in production agent systems or whether real-world trajectories behave like controlled canaries.

items.title: Robust Context-Aware Detection of Malicious Instructions in Text
items.dek: Context-aware detector of indirect prompt injection in LLM agents combines query-relative classification with adversarial training against evasion.
items.unproven: Evaluation methodology not specified; unclear which datasets, evasion strategies, or real agent deployments are covered; code availability not stated.

items.title: eMicro: Real-Time Multi-Hop Access Control for Microservices with eBPF
items.dek: eBPF-based system enforces multi-hop access control on microservices using DFA-encoded policies; tested on 12M workflows from Uber, Alibaba, ByteDance.
items.unproven: Deployed on proprietary production traces but no open-source code or reproducible evaluation; unclear whether policy language fits reader's existing SDLC controls or requires custom implementation.

items.title: Framework discloses data breach via Metabase 0-day
items.dek: Metabase 0-day exploited in Framework customer breach; warrants review of deployment settings.
items.unproven: whether the reader's organization uses Metabase or similar BI tools; remediation timeline

items.title: Mythos Attempted to Social Engineer Open Source Maintainer to Merge Malware
items.dek: Social engineering attack on open-source maintainer attempted merge of malware payload.
items.unproven: whether this affects the reader's dependency management process or SCA tool rules; scale of exposure

items.title: Zapscape (CVE-2026-64561): Guest-to-Host Escape in KVM/x86
items.dek: KVM/x86 guest-to-host escape discovered and published with PoC; hypervisor vendors must patch.
items.unproven: applicability to production deployments with standard mitigations (SMEP, SMAP, nested virt disabled) not established

items.title: DreamGuard: Efficient Runtime Guardrail for LLM Agents via Risk-Aware World Model
items.dek: DreamGuard proactive guardrail predicts multi-horizon risks for LLM agents via recurrent latent state and fused intervention signals.
items.unproven: Benchmarks on four synthetic tasks; does not establish robustness to adversarial agents or practical overhead in production SDLC integration.

items.title: Breaking Customized LLMs for Coding: Automated Red Teaming for Instruction Backdoor Attacks
items.dek: ARIA automated red-teaming framework generates covert backdoored instructions for customized LLMs across three code intelligence tasks.
items.unproven: Demonstrates attack feasibility on custom LLM platforms; does not establish detection or mitigation strategies for secure SDLC deployment.

items.title: LLMs won't break symmetric crypto
items.dek: LLMs lack the computational capacity to break symmetric cryptography; addresses a misconception in agent security threat modeling.
items.unproven: does not account for hybrid attacks, side channels, or deployment contexts where LLMs assist human cryptanalysts.

items.title: PromptShield Home: Ambient Multimodal Prompt Injection Defense for Smart-Home Agents
items.dek: Benchmark of multimodal prompt injection in smart-home agents reveals detectors over-block while LLMs over-refuse genuine commands.
items.unproven: Pilot benchmark on synthetic scenarios; no evidence that three-layer mediation strategy reaches production deployment or matches real-world ambient noise and occupancy patterns.

items.title: Dimension-Free Polylogarithmic Quantum Shadow Tomography from Sequential Pretty-Good Measurements
items.dek: Quantum shadow tomography achieves polylogarithmic sample complexity independent of state dimension, resolving an open question from 2018.
items.unproven: applicability to near-term quantum hardware; practical relevance to the reader's SDLC tooling and secure development processes

items.title: On Optimal Quantum Data Hiding and Maximal Separable Ball
items.dek: Optimal data-hiding ratios against separable and LOCC measurements proven to equal min{n,m} for bipartite systems.
items.unproven: relevance to classical application security or financial services systems the reader secures

items.title: Time-Reversal Selection Rules for Quantum Error Correction
items.dek: Time-reversal symmetry imposes parity selection rules on quantum error-correction codes, making even-weight error detection imply correction.
items.unproven: whether findings apply to error-correction schemes the reader must evaluate or deploy

items.title: Exponential logical-error reduction in quantum memories via optimal syndrome-measurement timing
items.dek: Optimal syndrome-measurement timing inversely proportional to code distance yields exponential logical-error reduction in quantum surface-code memories.
items.unproven: applicability to the reader's secure-SDLC processes or classical infrastructure; whether this affects SAST/DAST/SCA tooling decisions

items.title: Reversible Unlearnable Examples: Towards the Copyright Protection in Deep Learning Era
items.dek: Unlearnable examples with reversibility protect training data copyright; vocabulary for data-poison risk modeling.
items.unproven: robustness against adaptive attacks; generalization beyond vision tasks; feasibility in production ML pipelines.

items.title: A Note on the Influence of a Zero Length Nonce on GCM and GMAC
items.dek: Zero-length nonce in ISO/IEC GCM and GMAC allows hash-key recovery; NIST variant unaffected.
items.unproven: whether financial services deployments use ISO/IEC variant; impact scope limited to implementations that permit zero-length nonces.

items.title: MMAligner: Safeguarding Multimodal Large Language Models through Representation Calibration
items.dek: Multimodal LLM safety disparity traced to representation misalignment; calibration method proposed but no production deployment evidence.
items.unproven: applicability to proprietary LLMs used in agents; utility-safety trade-off measurement; generalization across model families and task domains.

items.title: RustGo: Fairly Directed Greybox Fuzzing for Enforcing Rust Memory Safety
items.dek: Rust-directed fuzzer prunes 78% of irrelevant paths by targeting unsafe code; fuzzing methodology, not SAST/DAST tooling integration.
items.unproven: integration into existing CI/CD fuzzing pipelines; performance on large codebases; memory-bug discovery rate versus standard greybox fuzzers.

items.title: An End-to-End Threat Model for the Quantum-as-a-Service Pipeline
items.dek: STRIDE threat model decomposed across six-stage QaaS pipeline identifies attack vectors and cross-stage chains.
items.unproven: Does not establish which attack chains are practically exploitable or what mitigations apply to real deployments.

items.title: On the Figures of Merit for Quantum Software Security: Toward a Benchmarking Rubric
items.dek: Proposes Security Figures of Merit for quantum software organized by ISO/IEC 25010 and QaaS pipeline layers.
items.unproven: Does not validate that proposed S-FoM set correlates with real security outcomes or inform tool selection.

items.title: ChainClaw: A Layered Agent Framework for Reliable On-Chain Execution
items.dek: ChainClaw agent framework addresses reactivity, irreversibility, and observability gaps in blockchain environments via layered architecture.
items.unproven: Evaluation on purpose-built benchmark; does not establish robustness against adversarial contracts or economic attacks in live deployment.

items.title: Provably Efficient Self-Calibrating Quantum Fault Tolerance
items.dek: Self-calibrating quantum fault tolerance with provable efficiency; addresses drift during long-running quantum computation.
items.unproven: proof assumes detection rate as calibration signal; no empirical validation on real quantum hardware; applicability to post-quantum cryptography migration timelines unclear

noise.title: Show HN: I spent 2 years designing a mechanical Magic Keyboard
noise.dek: Mechanical keyboard product launch; hardware design work unrelated to security or SDLC.

noise.title: Managing AI Coding Costs at Scale
noise.dek: Databricks cost-management patterns for AI coding tools; establishes vocabulary around token budgets and batching.
noise.unproven: applicability beyond Databricks' own infrastructure and use cases; no independent validation of claims

noise.title: Show HN: textlog – A quiet, text-only microblogging platform, open-source, no JS
noise.unproven: relevance to application security or secure SDLC
